The Truth About 5G - Journeyman Special [5780]

By: Chwayitisa Futshane | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What's driving the global anti-5G movement?

Summary:
As coronavirus continues to upend our lives, conspiracy theorists, tech giants and governments battle over the latest tech innovation. This report delves into the murky waters of 5G conspiracy theories.
Proponents of 5G promise it will transform our lives, from AI traffic control to downloads in seconds. 'This is where machines start talking to machines. And this is going to allow a revolution in the way we live and organise ourselves’. However, some activists claim it’s a health hazard. ‘I don't want to be a human lab rat. They're just using us to see if it's going to be okay’, says one Australian protester. With China leading the 5G race, some fear this spells the start of Chinese technological supremacy: 'China is eating America's lunch and the US is losing technological advantage. It is also losing influence', says Dr Huong Le Thu.

Activists claim 5G is an invisible and potentially deadly health hazard, blaming the radiation emitted by the technology for a range of long-term health problems.

"We are going to be in a radiation soup that we cannot opt out of. At the moment we have choices. Once 5G is implemented, we no longer have any choice." Activist leader

"There are just thousands and thousands of papers out there that have gone into everything from epidemiology of cancer to simple, does it make you feel bad, agitated, cause you symptoms of any form?" Professor

"5G's not just about phone calls and ever-increasing resolution of videos, it's going to unlock the Internet of Things. And this is where machines start talking to machines. And this is going to allow a whole revolution in the way we live and organise ourselves." Professor of engineering
Fears about 5G have prompted astonishing scenes around the world with telecommunication towers set on fire in multiple countries, including Australia.
The program investigates the rise of the anti-5G movement and the spread of wild conspiracy theories tying the COVID-19 pandemic to the 5G rollout. Piecing together the viral spread of these theories, the program uncovers a sophisticated misinformation campaign.
"It creates division. It creates disruptions. It creates protests. It creates possibly more people disobeying any lockdown orders, any social distancing orders. And of course, that then further damages the economy, damages the population in the first place by spreading the virus further." Digital media researcher
Security experts say the real and present danger around 5G is not the health concerns, but the deepening technological Cold War between the US and China, in which the contest for 5G supremacy is escalating.
"China is eating America's lunch. It is losing technological advantage; it is losing markets. It is losing also influence." National security researcher
This fascinating program provides valuable insight into one of the defining technological developments of our time.

metadata.Summary: As coronavirus continues to upend our lives, conspiracy theorists, tech giants and governments battle over the latest tech innovation. This report delves into the murky waters of 5G conspiracy theories. Proponents of 5G promise it will transform our lives, from AI traffic control to downloads in seconds. 'This is where machines start talking to machines. And this is going to allow a revolution in the way we live and organise ourselves’. However, some activists claim it’s a health hazard. ‘I don't want to be a human lab rat. They're just using us to see if it's going to be okay’, says one Australian protester. With China leading the 5G race, some fear this spells the start of Chinese technological supremacy: 'China is eating America's lunch and the US is losing technological advantage. It is also losing influence', says Dr Huong Le Thu.
